long_biography.plain_text:
Soitec grew from Auberton-Hervé's conviction that silicon-on-insulator research could become an industrial materials business. A physicist at CEA-Leti, he and Jean-Michel Lamure left the laboratory in 1992 to co-found the company around Smart Cut technology. They moved from a pilot line to volume production, licensed the process to Shin-Etsu and floated the company in Paris seven years later.

Auberton-Hervé spent twenty-three years directing strategy, operations and finance as Soitec added manufacturing sites in Europe, Asia and the United States. He also helped organise the wider industry, chairing the SOI Industry Consortium and SEMI International. After executive management, he created 4A Consulting & Engineering and took operating, advisory and board roles that put his semiconductor experience to work in scaling other technology companies.
